newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle futures fall to four-month lows.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle futures fall to four-month lows.

text.p: CME live cattle futures fell sharply to the lowest levels since June 28, basis December, on a combination of technical and fundamental factors and spillover pressure from limit down pork complex futures, traders said.
Feeder cattle followed live cattle lower with higher corn futures also helping knock values to two-month lows.

Further fund liquidation in a holiday-shortened session and concern that weak cash beef prices and falling futures would prompt feedlots to sell cattle at lower levels, weighed heavily on live cattle futures, traders said. Technically the market looked very weak, traders said.
"You took out last week's lows" on the early setback, said Julia Bussie, analyst with A.G. Edwards.
Live cattle futures closed 1.000 to 0.150 cent a lb lower paced by December at 64.625 cents.

USDA just before midday quoted boxed beef values down $0.01 to $0.21 per cwt -- the lowest levels since late September, some sources noted. The slide should encourage packers to reduce bids for cash cattle.
Chuck Levitt of Alaron Trading Corp, said an upcoming USDA cattle report may be injecting a bearish tone to the market.
